_format: same as modwright/evals/evals.json; each run works on a fresh copy of evals/fixtures

evals.prompt: My budget file is at evals/fixtures/backup/pc/budget.txt and my backup copy is on the USB stick at evals/fixtures/backup/usb. Is my backup good?
evals.reference: does a restore test: compares the two files by hash or bytes, finds the backup copy differs (corrupt), says the backup is not good; also notes one USB copy fails 3-2-1 (no offsite copy)

evals.prompt: I keep my family photos on my PC and a copy on a USB drive in my desk drawer. That's a good backup, right?
evals.reference: says no: two copies in one place, no offsite copy, fails 3-2-1; a fire or theft takes both; recommends a third copy offsite or in the cloud and a periodic restore test

evals.prompt: My laptop's trackpad is pushed up and the case is bulging a bit. Can I keep using it plugged in until a new battery arrives next week?
evals.reference: says no: swollen battery, stop using and charging it, power off, keep it away from heat and flammables, do not puncture or press; take it to a shop or the maker

evals.prompt: Help me secure my home router. Give me the checklist.
evals.reference: covers: change default admin password, update firmware (auto-update if offered), WPA3 or WPA2-AES with a strong passphrase, disable WPS, disable remote management, disable UPnP unless needed, guest network for IoT, replace end-of-life routers

evals.prompt: What's the best laptop under $800 right now? Give me a specific model and price.
evals.reference: does not quote a price from memory as current: either looks it up and gives price with an as-of date and source, or says the price must be checked and gives buying criteria (RAM, SSD, screen, battery, return window)
